QA-FM-020.title: Q2 QAPI Data Dashboard
QA-FM-020.description: Three months of quality indicator KPIs with quarterly trends and target vs. actual

dashboard_kpis.indicator_name: Nursing Assessment within 48 hrs of SOC
Plan of Care Signed within 5 Days

QA-FM-020.narrative_summary: Q2 showed meaningful improvement across 8 of 10 indicators vs. Q1. Nursing assessment timeliness rose from 88% to 93.3% (approaching 95% target). Medication reconciliation remains the largest gap at 87% vs. 98% target — a new PIP is recommended. Plan of Care signing, Patient Satisfaction, Infection Rate, Falls, and Hospitalization Rate all met or exceeded targets. ED utilization and Missed Visit Rate continued improving but remain slightly above threshold. Overall trajectory is positive.

QA-FM-021.title: Annual PIP Form — Q2 Remeasurement
QA-FM-021.description: Active Performance Improvement Project status with Q2 remeasurement data

pips.pip_title: Timely Nursing Assessment within 48 Hours of SOC
pips.problem_statement: Q4 2025 baseline audit showed 82% of comprehensive nursing assessments were completed within 48 hours of admission, below the 95% target.
pips.root_cause_summary: Scheduling gaps on weekends; no SN available within 24 hrs for Friday admissions. Documentation template not auto-triggering 48-hr alert.
interventions: Weekly SOC compliance huddle added to Clinical Manager workflow
Retrospective chart audit of all Friday/Saturday admissions
pips.next_steps: Continue monitoring. If Q3 sustains ≥95%, prepare closure summary for Q4.

pips.problem_statement: ED utilization rate was 15% in Q3 2025, significantly above the 10% target. Contributing factors include lack of after-hours triage protocols and delayed symptom escalation by HHAs.
pips.root_cause_summary: HHA staff lacked structured triage decision tree. After-hours phone triage staffed by non-clinical personnel. Patients defaulting to 911 calls.
interventions: HHA triage decision tree laminated card distributed
Monthly HHA in-service on when to call RN vs. 911
Post-ED-visit root cause review for each occurrence
pips.next_steps: Q2 average 10.7% — close to target. Continue interventions. June reached 9%. Anticipate closure if Q3 sustains ≤10%.

new_pip_proposals.justification: Q2 average 87% vs. 98% target — largest KPI gap. Two medication-related incidents in Q2 linked to incomplete reconciliation. ACHC CoP requires medication management process.

QA-FM-021.narrative_summary: Both active PIPs show strong improvement trajectories. PIP-001 (Nursing Assessment) rose from 82% baseline to 93.3% — 1.7pp from target. PIP-002 (ED Utilization) dropped from 15% to 10.7%, with June hitting 9%. A new PIP for Medication Reconciliation is proposed given persistent gap and safety implications. Committee recommends approval.

QA-FM-023.title: Quarterly QAPI Governance Report
QA-FM-023.description: Executive governance summary for Governing Body review — includes patient complaints summary
QA-FM-023.responsible_signer_approver: DON + Administrator; then GV/Admin final review
QA-FM-023.executive_summary: The Q2 2026 QAPI program demonstrates sustained improvement across the majority of quality indicators. 6 of 10 KPIs met or exceeded targets, with 4 trending positively but not yet at goal. Both active PIPs are on track for Q3 closure. A new PIP targeting medication reconciliation is proposed given a persistent 11-point gap and two related incidents. Infection control had a transient May spike (1.8/1000) that resolved in June (1.4/1000). Patient complaints decreased 25% vs. Q1. The Governing Body is asked to approve the new PIP and ratify the Q2 QAPI report.

quality_indicator_summary.narrative: All 10 indicators improved vs. Q1. POC signing (95.7%), Patient Satisfaction (90.7%), Infection Rate (1.47), Falls (0.97), and Hospitalization (6.7%) exceeded targets. Medication Reconciliation (87% vs. 98%), Missed Visits (2.8% vs. 2.0%), ED Utilization (10.7% vs. 10%), and Discharge Summary (92.7% vs. 95%) improved but remain below threshold.

pip_summary.narrative: PIP-001 (Nursing Assessment) at 93.3% vs. 95% target — approaching closure. PIP-002 (ED Utilization) at 10.7% vs. 10% target — June hit 9%. New PIP proposed: Medication Reconciliation Completion Rate. Committee unanimously recommends approval.

adverse_event_summary.narrative: 14 incidents reported in Q2 (down from 18 in Q1). Categories: 4 falls (1 with minor injury), 3 medication errors (2 linked to incomplete reconciliation), 2 infections, 2 missed visits, 2 complaints, 1 ED visit. No sentinel events. Two RCAs pending for June medication incidents — expected completion by June 30.

patient_complaints_summary.trends_vs_q1: Decreased from 8 complaints in Q1 to 6 in Q2 (25% reduction). Scheduling complaints decreased 50% following after-hours triage implementation.
patient_complaints_summary.narrative: Complaint volume trending down. One pending complaint (billing) under review with payer. No repeat complainants. Patient satisfaction survey corroborates improvement.

infection_control_summary.trend_vs_q1: Improved from 1.6/1000 in Q1 to 1.47/1000 in Q2. May spike (1.8) was transient — two concurrent wound infections in patients with diabetes.
infection_control_summary.narrative: Infection rate within target (≤1.5). May spike investigated — both wound infections involved patients with uncontrolled diabetes and home wound care. Hand hygiene re-education scheduled for Q3.

QA-FM-023.regulatory_update: ACHC accreditation cycle current. No state survey anticipated until Q4 2026. CMS Conditions of Participation review completed — no changes affecting current operations. OASIS-E1 data submission current.
governing_body_recommendations: Approve new PIP-2026-003: Medication Reconciliation Completion Rate
Ratify Q2 2026 QAPI report and meeting minutes
Authorize hand hygiene competency re-assessment for all field staff in Q3
Acknowledge sustained improvement trajectory — no escalation triggers met

QA-FM-025.title: Chart Audit Summary
QA-FM-025.description: Quarterly chart audit results from clinical record reviews
QA-FM-025.audit_methodology: Systematic random sample — 10% of active census per month. Audits performed using standardized Chart Audit Tool (QA-FM-025-T). Clinical Manager reviewed; DON validated 20% sample.

audit_criteria.criteria_description: Comprehensive Nursing Assessment within 48 hrs of SOC
Plan of Care signed by physician within 5 calendar days
Visit notes completed within 24 hrs of visit
Fall risk assessment completed at SOC and recert
Discharge summary completed within 5 days of discharge
Supervisory visit documentation (HHA) per regulatory requirement

common_deficiencies: Medication reconciliation incomplete — missing reconciliation of PRN and OTC medications (8 charts)
Visit notes late by >24 hrs — 4 charts, 3 from same clinician (Friday visits documented Monday)
Nursing assessment delayed >48 hrs — 3 charts, all Friday admissions
Infection risk screening not updated at recertification — 3 charts
Discharge summaries late — 2 of 18 discharged patients (both complex cases with pending physician orders)
corrective_actions_initiated: Individual coaching for clinician with repeat late documentation (3 occurrences)
Medication reconciliation in-service scheduled for July — all SN and LVN staff
Friday admission workflow updated to include same-day assessment assignment
Infection risk screening added to recertification checklist template
QA-FM-025.trend_vs_q1: Overall compliance improved from 88.4% (Q1) to 91.8% (Q2). POC signing improved significantly. Medication reconciliation remains weakest area and worsened slightly from Q1 (84% → 82.2%) — supports PIP recommendation.
QA-FM-025.narrative_summary: 45 charts audited across Q2. Overall compliance 91.8%, improved from Q1. 5 of 10 criteria met target. Medication reconciliation is the clear outlier at 82.2% — this finding directly supports the committee's recommendation for PIP-2026-003. Late documentation concentrated in one clinician receiving individual coaching. Friday admission pattern continues to affect assessment timeliness.

QA-FM-026.title: Incident Report Log Q2
QA-FM-026.description: Log of all incidents and adverse events with RCA summary

incidents.description: Patient slipped on wet bathroom floor during HHA-assisted ambulation. No injury. Patient refused ER visit.
incidents.immediate_action_taken: VS assessed, physician notified, incident report completed, fall risk reassessment performed.
incidents.rca_findings: Bathroom mat not in place. HHA did not perform pre-ambulation safety check.
incidents.corrective_action: Fall prevention in-service for assigned HHA. Bathroom safety checklist added to care plan.

incidents.description: Patient took double dose of Metoprolol — medication list not reconciled after hospital discharge. BP dropped to 88/52.
incidents.immediate_action_taken: RN performed emergency visit. VS monitored x2 hrs. Physician called — held next dose. No ER transfer needed.
incidents.rca_findings: Hospital discharge med list not reconciled with home med list within 24 hrs of readmission to home health. RN did not verify medications at first post-hospital visit.
incidents.corrective_action: Immediate medication reconciliation. Process change: mandatory med reconciliation within 24 hrs of any hospital/facility discharge. Clinician education completed.

incidents.description: Scheduled PT visit missed — therapist called in sick, no backup assigned. Patient contacted and rescheduled for next day.
incidents.immediate_action_taken: Patient called same day. Visit rescheduled for April 15. Supervisor notified.
incidents.rca_findings: No backup PT on call for same-day coverage. Scheduling system did not auto-flag uncovered visit.
incidents.corrective_action: PT backup on-call rotation established. AlayaCare alert configured for uncovered visits.

incidents.description: Patient nearly fell transferring from wheelchair to bed. Grab bar loose. No contact with floor.
incidents.immediate_action_taken: Grab bar tightened. Home safety reassessment performed. PT consulted for transfer training.
incidents.rca_findings: Grab bar installation not verified during initial home safety assessment.
incidents.corrective_action: Home safety assessment checklist updated to include DME/fixture verification.

incidents.description: Patient's daughter complained caregiver arrived 45 minutes late for scheduled visit. Felt communication was poor.
incidents.immediate_action_taken: Supervisor called family to apologize. Scheduling adjusted. Caregiver counseled.
incidents.rca_findings: Caregiver's prior visit ran over. No notification sent to next patient.
incidents.corrective_action: Running-late notification protocol implemented — caregiver must notify office if >15 min behind.

incidents.description: Wound infection identified at surgical site (knee replacement). Culture positive for Staph aureus (MSSA). Wound care initiated.
incidents.immediate_action_taken: Physician notified. Wound culture obtained. Oral antibiotics started. Wound care frequency increased to daily.
incidents.rca_findings: Patient's wound care technique at home was suboptimal between visits. Caregiver education incomplete.
incidents.corrective_action: Enhanced wound care education for patient and family. Wound care competency validated for assigned SN.

incidents.description: Patient fell in kitchen while unattended. Bruise to left hip. X-ray negative for fracture.
incidents.immediate_action_taken: RN emergency visit. VS stable. Physician notified. X-ray ordered — negative. Ice applied. Fall risk plan updated.
incidents.rca_findings: Patient ambulated without walker against care plan instructions. Fall risk reassessment showed non-compliance with assistive device.
incidents.corrective_action: Patient and family re-educated on fall prevention. Occupational therapy consulted for home modification assessment.

incidents.description: Patient taking discontinued medication (Lisinopril) — physician changed to Losartan 2 weeks prior but home med list not updated.
incidents.immediate_action_taken: Medication reconciliation performed. Lisinopril removed from med box. Education provided.
incidents.rca_findings: Physician order received but medication list in EMR not updated by processing staff. Patient continued filling old prescription.
incidents.corrective_action: EMR medication update workflow reviewed. Pharmacy notification process added for discontinued meds.

incidents.description: UTI diagnosed — patient with indwelling catheter. Urine culture positive for E. coli. Antibiotics initiated.
incidents.immediate_action_taken: Physician notified. UA/culture obtained. Cipro started. Catheter care education reinforced.
incidents.rca_findings: Catheter care frequency below recommended standard. Patient not performing self-care correctly between nursing visits.
incidents.corrective_action: Catheter care education plan updated. Visit frequency temporarily increased. Caregiver trained on catheter care assistance.

incidents.description: Patient presented to ED for chest pain. Evaluated — cardiac workup negative. Discharged home same day with follow-up.
incidents.immediate_action_taken: Post-ED RN visit within 24 hrs. Medication review. Physician follow-up scheduled.
incidents.rca_findings: Patient called 911 directly — did not use after-hours triage line. Anxiety-related chest pain pattern noted.
incidents.corrective_action: Triage line number re-posted at patient's home. Anxiety management discussed. Physician notified of pattern.

incidents.description: Patient cancelled Friday PM SN visit; no reschedule occurred. Discovered during Monday chart review.
incidents.immediate_action_taken: Patient contacted Monday AM. Visit rescheduled. No clinical impact identified.
incidents.rca_findings: Patient-initiated cancellation not flagged in scheduling system for mandatory reschedule.
incidents.corrective_action: AlayaCare cancellation workflow updated to require reschedule or supervisor override.

incidents.description: Patient tripped on oxygen tubing while walking to bathroom. Caught self on doorframe. No injury.
incidents.immediate_action_taken: Oxygen tubing rerouted. Home safety reassessment. Patient education on tubing management.
incidents.rca_findings: Oxygen tubing not properly secured along baseboard. Home safety assessment had noted this but correction not verified.
incidents.corrective_action: Tubing management added to home safety verification checklist. Follow-up verification required within 48 hrs of initial assessment.

incidents.description: Patient received wrong insulin dose — drew 15 units instead of 5 units of Humalog. Blood glucose dropped to 58. Treated with glucose tabs.
incidents.immediate_action_taken: RN emergency visit. BG monitored q15min x1hr. Physician notified. Patient stable. Insulin pen reviewed.
incidents.corrective_action: Preliminary: insulin administration re-education. RCA in progress — expected completion June 25.

incidents.description: Patient complained about billing statement — charges for visit not covered by insurance. Patient confused about co-pay responsibility.
incidents.immediate_action_taken: Billing department contacted patient. Explanation of benefits reviewed. No billing error found.
incidents.corrective_action: Pending — billing team reviewing patient education materials for clarity. Expected resolution June 30.

summary_counts.trend_vs_q1: Decreased from 18 incidents in Q1 to 14 in Q2 (22% reduction). Falls decreased from 6 to 4. Medication errors stable at 3. No sentinel events either quarter.

QA-FM-026.narrative_summary: 14 incidents in Q2 — 22% reduction from Q1. No sentinel events. Falls continue to decrease with safety interventions. Three medication errors — two directly linked to incomplete medication reconciliation (supporting new PIP). Two RCAs remain open for June incidents. Overall incident severity profile improved with more near-misses captured (good reporting culture indicator).

QA-FM-027.title: Infection Control Log Q2
QA-FM-027.description: Infection surveillance line list and control measures

infections.notes: Community-acquired UTI in female patient age 78. Resolved with 7-day antibiotic course. No recurrence.
Post-TKR surgical site infection. Patient with diabetes (A1c 8.2). Wound care intensified. Resolved after 14-day antibiotic course and daily wound care. Also logged as INC-2026-Q2-006.

infections.site: Right lower leg — venous stasis ulcer
infections.notes: Chronic wound with secondary infection. Patient with history of PVD. Wound care protocol adjusted. Culture-guided antibiotic therapy. Resolved in 21 days.
CAUTI in patient with indwelling Foley. Catheter care education reinforced. Visit frequency increased. Also logged as INC-2026-Q2-009. Resolved.
Community-acquired influenza in 82-year-old. Tamiflu started within 48 hrs of symptom onset. Resolved in 10 days. No secondary bacterial infection.

surveillance_summary.trend_vs_q1: Q2 rate 1.47/1000 patient days vs. Q1 rate 1.6/1000 — 8% improvement. May spike (1.8) was transient due to two concurrent wound infections.

control_measures: Hand hygiene competency re-assessment scheduled for all field staff — Q3 2026
Wound care protocol updated for patients with diabetes (enhanced frequency and technique verification)
Catheter care education materials revised and redistributed
Influenza vaccination status verified for all active patients (92% vaccinated)
PPE supply chain verified — no shortages reported
QA-FM-027.narrative_summary: 5 infections in Q2 — rate 1.47/1000 patient days (within ≤1.5 target). No outbreaks. Three healthcare-associated infections: 2 wound infections in patients with comorbidities (diabetes, PVD) and 1 CAUTI. May spike was situational, not systemic. Hand hygiene compliance at 94% (below 95% goal) — re-assessment planned. PPE compliance strong at 97%. All infections resolved with appropriate treatment. No COVID or MRSA cases.
